source: Pirolli & Card (2005) The sensemaking process and leverage points for analyst technology as identified through cognitive task analysis
finding: Sensemaking is gathering information, re-representing it in a schema, building insight by manipulating that representation, and making a product or action. The paper gives a notional model with two nested loops: a foraging loop and a sensemaking loop.
numbers: Formula in paper: information gathering, then re-representation in schema, then insight from manipulation, then knowledge product or direct action.
quote: a foraging loop that involves processes aimed at seeking information, searching and filtering it, and reading and extracting information
limits: Conference paper, 'broad brush' and 'first results'. It states no number of analysts, no hours, no counts. It is a notional model, not a tested one.
agent_relevance: Our S-states should keep two loops apart: one that fetches and filters evidence, one that fits evidence to a model. Mixing them hides which one failed.

source: Pirolli & Card (2005) The sensemaking process and leverage points for analyst technology as identified through cognitive task analysis
finding: The data flow has fixed stores: external data sources, shoebox (relevant subset), evidence file (snippets), schema, hypotheses, presentation. Circles are processes: search and filter, read and extract, schematize, build case, tell story.
numbers: Six data stores, in order: external data, shoebox, evidence file, schema, hypotheses, presentation.
limits: Stores are described from the figure text; the figure itself is not machine-readable here. The model is approximate.
agent_relevance: Template for agent memory: raw pool, small kept subset, snippet file with provenance, organised schema, hypothesis list, output. Each store can be a separate, code-managed object.

source: Pirolli & Card (2005) The sensemaking process and leverage points for analyst technology as identified through cognitive task analysis
finding: Process runs both bottom-up (data to theory) and top-down (theory to data) in an opportunistic mix. Top-down: a presentation can trigger re-evaluation, new evidence search, new hypotheses, and re-checking of basic facts.
numbers: Back loops exist at every level; no frequency of loop use is reported.
limits: Opportunistic mixing is observed, not measured. No count of how often each direction fires.
agent_relevance: The agent should allow backward edges (hypothesis to new search; schema failure to re-read raw data), but code, not the model, should trigger them on a signal (G1).

source: Pirolli & Card (2005) The sensemaking process and leverage points for analyst technology as identified through cognitive task analysis
finding: Foraging trades off three things under deadline or overload: exploring more of the space (recall), enriching by narrowing to smaller higher-precision sets, and exploiting items by deeper reading. Analysts started with broad sets and narrowed in steps before reading (after Patterson et al.).
numbers: Three processes: explore, enrich, exploit. Linked to the precision-recall trade-off. Figure 5 shows successive narrowing rings.
limits: Qualitative. The trade-off is argued from CTA and from Patterson, Roth and Woods 2001, not shown with data in this paper.
agent_relevance: Maps onto retrieve wide, rank, then read deeply. A budget split across explore/enrich/exploit can be a code parameter; the model does not choose it.

source: Pirolli & Card (2005) The sensemaking process and leverage points for analyst technology as identified through cognitive task analysis
finding: Cost-structure view: expert analysts set filters low (accept more noise) so as not to miss faint signals, but reject unimportant items faster than novices because of prior and tacit knowledge. So experts get more relevant information in less time.
numbers: Figure 6 plots information gained against time for expert vs less expert; no figures given in the text.
limits: Claim rests on a hypothetical curve, not data. 'Faster rejection' is asserted from observation.
agent_relevance: For retrieval screening: loose threshold plus a cheap fast reject step is the expert pattern. A cheap filter pass before expensive reading matches it.

source: Pirolli & Card (2005) The sensemaking process and leverage points for analyst technology as identified through cognitive task analysis
finding: Sensemaking-side pain points: problem structuring (generating and managing hypotheses), evidentiary reasoning (marshalling evidence for and against), and decision making. Working-memory limits cap how many hypotheses, evidence items and relations can be heeded together; the paper says reasoning about evidence has an exponential cost structure.
numbers: Claim: number of relations among data 'can grow rapidly' (social links among suspects). No exact growth figure.
quote: Reasoning about evidence and hypotheses has an exponential cost structure.
limits: Exponential growth is stated from verbal protocols, not fitted. Offloading to visual displays is proposed, not tested.
agent_relevance: LLM context is a working-memory limit too. Offload hypotheses and evidence relations to an external structured store and re-read only what a check needs.

source: Pirolli & Card (2005) The sensemaking process and leverage points for analyst technology as identified through cognitive task analysis
finding: Named bias leverage points: perception is biased toward existing schemas; people fail to generate hypotheses, fail to weigh diagnosticity of evidence, and fail to focus on disconfirmation. Proposed lever: shift analyst attention to highly diagnostic evidence and to the search for disconfirming relations.
numbers: No effect size. Cites Tversky and Kahneman 1974 for the bias set.
limits: Proposal only. The paper has no tool test.
agent_relevance: Supports G3: a pass must come from evidence the answer was not fitted to. Code can rank evidence by diagnosticity (how well it separates hypotheses) and force a look at disconfirming items.

source: Pirolli & Card (2005) The sensemaking process and leverage points for analyst technology as identified through cognitive task analysis
finding: Expertise grounding: analysts show domain schemas, as in chess (Simon and Chase 1973: master skill from patterns built over about 15,000 hours) and Klein's recognition-primed decisions. Experts select and re-encode information into special representations that allow planning and reasoning.
numbers: 15,000 hours chess figure quoted from Simon and Chase 1973 as cited by this paper. Earlier business-analyst case (Pirolli & Card 1999) found schemas around market players, application opportunities, market development, report types.
limits: Single-expert case study for the 1999 finding. Chess figure is a citation, not tested here.
agent_relevance: Schema is the unit of expertise. An agent scaffold should hold named, reusable schemas per task type, not free text.

source: Russell, Stefik, Pirolli & Card (1993) The cost structure of sensemaking
finding: Learning loop complex: generation loop (find a good representation), data coverage loop (encode data into it), residue (items that do not fit), representation shift loop (change the representation for better coverage). Cited by P&C 2005 as the base of the sense loop.
numbers: None verified this session. P&C 2005 text describes the four loops.
limits: Not opened. Known only through the P&C 2005 description. The original was a case on a printer-repair curriculum.
agent_relevance: Residue-driven representation change is a code-checkable trigger: count items that do not fit the schema; shift the frame only when residue passes a threshold.

source: Pirolli & Card (1999) Information foraging, Psychological Review 106(4)
finding: Information foraging theory: people shape their activity to maximise information gained per unit cost, in patches linked by information scent. Used by P&C 2005 as the foraging loop and for the explore/enrich/exploit cost structure.
numbers: No numbers verified this session.
limits: Not opened. Described only via citations in P&C 2005, InForage (2025) and DeepNews (2025). Do not quote its effect sizes without opening it.
agent_relevance: The foraging half of our schema can borrow the rate-of-gain rule: stop a source when marginal gain per cost falls below the average.

source: Klein, Moon & Hoffman (2006) Making sense of sensemaking 1; Klein et al. data/frame theory
finding: Rival account: a frame defines what counts as data, and sensemaking elaborates, questions or replaces frames. P&C 2005 says it plays a role like its schema. Lebiere et al. 2013 note P&C used a similar model.
numbers: None verified.
limits: Not opened here. Covered in the parallel subfield 'Sensemaking, data-frame model'; only the link is noted.
agent_relevance: Link only. See sibling subfield on data-frame theory.

source: Lebiere, Pirolli, Thomson, Paik, Rutledge-Taylor, Staszewski, Anderson (2013) A functional model of sensemaking in a neurocognitive architecture
finding: ACT-R model of the foraging and hypothesis-updating core of sensemaking on six IARPA ICArUS 'AHA' tasks (map-based probability estimation from event reports, then feature layers HUMINT/IMINT/MOVINT/SIGINT/SOCINT). It predicted the presence and degree of four biases without engineering them: confirmation, anchoring and adjustment, representativeness (base-rate neglect), probability matching.
numbers: Six tasks; original human dataset N=45 participants; generalisation sample N=103 Penn State students (graduate Geospatial Intelligence Certificate coursework).
limits: Artificial geospatial data and a narrow probability task. Fits are about the task, not the full open-ended analyst process P&C described. Model has free parameters and strategy choices.
agent_relevance: Strong source for the idea that biases come from task structure plus architecture limits plus strategy. Bias mitigation should be built from those three levers, not from 'be careful' prompts.

source: Lebiere, Pirolli, Thomson, Paik, Rutledge-Taylor, Staszewski, Anderson (2013) A functional model of sensemaking in a neurocognitive architecture
finding: Bias definitions: confirmation bias is a probability distribution peakier than the Bayesian optimum; anchoring is flatter than optimum (insufficient move from the uniform prior). Biases arise from mechanisms: blended retrieval, partial matching, and early utility-based layer selection (for example picking SIGINT too early).
numbers: Table 6 (novel Penn State data, model vs human). S1 scores (match to Bayesian rational): T1 81.7 vs 80.7; T2 68.5 vs 78.9; T3 72.1 vs 79.7; T4 94.4 vs 87.6; T5 84.5 vs 84.5; T6 85.3 vs 88.3. S2 (resource allocation) T3 34.7 vs 73.8, a clear model miss.
limits: Paper says trial-by-trial S1 fits were weaker on the new sample and the model missed some strategy of the Penn State group (more educated, more rational).
agent_relevance: Operational, measurable bias definition (distribution sharpness vs Bayes) that we can apply to an LLM's stated probabilities over hypotheses.

source: Lebiere, Pirolli, Thomson, Paik, Rutledge-Taylor, Staszewski, Anderson (2013) A functional model of sensemaking in a neurocognitive architecture
finding: Reinforcement learning of a preference order for intelligence layers; negative feedback on winner-take-all allocation in Tasks 1-3 leads to probability matching in Tasks 4-6. Confirmation bias in weighing evidence appears when probability adjustment on small values over-adjusts.
numbers: Resource allocation was forced choice: 100 percent to one category in Tasks 1-3.
limits: Mechanisms are model internals; human evidence is only the behaviour match above.
agent_relevance: Shows feedback history can shift strategy. For an agent: give outcomes of earlier choices in code, rather than ask it to reflect.

source: Andrews (2011) Space to Think: Sensemaking and Large, High-Resolution Displays (PhD dissertation, Virginia Tech); includes Andrews, Endert & North (2010)
finding: Study 1: 8 students solved the VAST 2006 'Stegosaurus' scenario (230 simulated news stories plus images, a map, a spreadsheet; about 10 of 238 documents give ground truth; a red herring) on a small 17-inch display (S1-S4) or a 33-megapixel 8-monitor wall (L1-L4). No significant differences in time or correctness.
numbers: N=8. Fastest solution just under 1.5 hours, slowest close to 3.5 hours. Scores varied widely, from near perfect to poor. Subject L1 spent the first 45 minutes laying out space.
limits: Tiny N and huge variance; null result is underpowered. No think-aloud used, to avoid interference.
agent_relevance: Same kind of task (document pile, hidden plot, red herring) as agent benchmarks. Large between-person variance means single runs are unreliable: use many runs.

source: Andrews (2011) Space to Think: Sensemaking and Large, High-Resolution Displays (PhD dissertation, Virginia Tech); includes Andrews, Endert & North (2010)
finding: Behaviour differed by display though score did not. Small-display users paged through maximised windows (thrashing) and kept paper notes of keywords, names, questions, leads, theories. Large-display users laid out documents and made digital notes. Notes map to stages of the P&C loop.
numbers: Study 2: 5 government-lab participants (4 practising analysts, 1 tool developer); observational, no comparison.
limits: Mapping notes to P&C stages is the author's interpretation. Small sample.
agent_relevance: The shoebox and evidence file appear as real artefacts people make. Our evidence file should keep snippets with source pointers, as the analysts' notes did.

source: Andrews (2011) Space to Think: Sensemaking and Large, High-Resolution Displays (PhD dissertation, Virginia Tech); includes Andrews, Endert & North (2010)
finding: Study 3 compared large and small displays with a spatial workspace. Large-display users built more and richer structures; the gain in analytic performance was not significant.
numbers: Table 4.1 (large vs small): structures 15.75 vs 9 (p=0.004); structural events 96.9 vs 45.3 (p=0.011); complex structures 4.35 vs 0.875 (p=0.065); share complex 29.7% vs 7.7% (p=0.086); coverage 18.53% vs 13.12% (p=0.061); span 52.26% vs 34.39% (p=0.095). Unpaired two-tailed t-tests with alpha set at p<0.1.
limits: Exploratory, alpha 0.1, small N, many tests with no correction. Analytic performance not significantly better.
agent_relevance: More externalised structure did not raise accuracy here. Warns against assuming a richer schema store alone improves answers; need a check on correctness.

source: Pirolli & Card (2005) slide summary (C. Rojo, Stony Brook CSE591)
finding: Student slide summary of the P&C paper. It restates the two-loop model and the leverage points. Used only to cross-check the primary text.
numbers: None beyond the primary.
limits: Secondary slides; text extraction was lossy. The primary paper was used for all claims.
agent_relevance: None beyond the primary.

source: Patterson, Roth & Woods (2001) Predicting vulnerabilities in computer-supported inferential analysis under data overload
finding: Observed that analysts start with broad document sets and narrow stepwise to smaller sets before reading. P&C 2005 uses this for the foraging loop.
numbers: None verified.
limits: Not opened. Known through P&C 2005.
agent_relevance: Evidence for wide-then-narrow retrieval before deep reading.

source: Kang & Stasko and related analyst field studies (cited by Andrews 2011)
finding: Andrews (2011) cites Kang et al. for an 'overview, filter, detail' style of investigation. The point recorded here is that analysts do not follow one fixed order.
numbers: None verified.
limits: Not opened; recorded only because Andrews (2011) cites it. Do not treat as verified.
agent_relevance: Do not hard-code one strict loop order; keep entry points flexible.

source: Suh, Min, Palani & Xia (2023) Sensecape: Enabling multilevel exploration and sensemaking with large language models (UIST '23)
finding: Sensecape is an LLM interface built to let users switch between foraging and sensemaking (cites P&C 2005), using canvases, hierarchical zoom and LLM-generated subtopics. Within-subject study, Sensecape vs a ChatGPT-like baseline with a canvas.
numbers: N=12 (age M=26.9). Prompts issued: 7.3 vs 5.8 (n.s., p=0.37). Nodes: 26.8 vs 23.5 (n.s.). Concepts explored: 68.3 (SD 49.1) vs 22.8 (SD 7.7), t(11)=3.1, p=0.01. Hierarchy levels: 4.3 vs 2.6, t(11)=2.7, p=0.02. Revisits: 12.8 vs 0.7, t(11)=3.8.
limits: Small N, student-heavy sample, self-chosen tasks, no accuracy ground truth. Measures are activity counts, not correctness of understanding. Inter-rater ICC 0.93 on concept counts.
agent_relevance: Same prompts but about 3x concepts: structure raises coverage, not just chat volume. Evidence that the foraging-sense switch helps humans using LLMs; it does not test an autonomous agent.

source: Liu, Wu et al. (2023/2024) Selenite: Scaffolding online sensemaking with comprehensive overviews elicited from LLMs
finding: An LLM extracts options and criteria from pages to give an up-front overview; cites P&C 2005 for sensemaking. Users read faster and externalised more valid criteria.
numbers: Study 2, within-subject N=12: time 840.3 s (SD 102.7) vs 1319.3 s (SD 120.0), 36.3% faster, F(1,20)=102.5, p<0.01; valid criteria 12.93 vs 6.79 (+90.4%, p<0.01); precision 98.8% vs 78.4%, recall 73.0% vs 30.4% (p<0.05); extra searches 2.01 vs 0.33. Option extraction 100% accurate in the accuracy study. Study 3 open case N=8.
limits: Shopping-type tasks on 2 given pages (about 15 screens each); small N; ground-truth criteria curated by the authors. 3 of 8 case participants worried about GPT-4 hallucination.
agent_relevance: A cheap overview step before deep reading (enrich before exploit) raised recall of key criteria by 42.6 points in humans. Candidate pre-read step for the agent, with a check against invented criteria.

source: Edge, Trinh, Cheng, Bradley, Chao, Mody, Truitt, Metropolitansky, Ness & Larson (2024) From local to global: a Graph RAG approach to query-focused summarization
finding: Defines 'global sensemaking questions' over a whole corpus (about 1 million tokens) that vector RAG cannot answer. GraphRAG builds an entity graph, detects communities, writes community summaries, then answers by map-reduce. GPT-4 judge compares comprehensiveness, diversity, empowerment, directness.
numbers: Two corpora (podcast transcripts; news). Graph sizes: podcast 8,564 nodes / 20,691 edges; news 15,754 nodes / 19,520 edges. Global methods beat vector RAG: comprehensiveness win rate 72-83% (p<.001) podcast, 72-80% news; diversity 75-82% and 62-71%. Root-level summaries (C0) used over 97% fewer tokens than source-text summarisation and kept 72% and 62% win rates over vector RAG. Vs source-text summarisation, low-level summaries won 57-64% on comprehensiveness. Vector RAG gave the most direct answers.
limits: LLM-as-judge with no gold answers; empowerment results mixed; indexing is expensive; two corpora only; GPT-4 only. Judge not human-validated in what was read.
agent_relevance: Supports a hierarchical schema layer (community summaries) as the bridge from foraging to sense on large pools. Judging by an LLM is weak evidence under G5.

source: Singh, Tariq, Jalalvand, Chhetri, Nepal, Paris & Lochner (2025) LLMs in the SOC: an empirical study of human-AI collaboration in security operations centres
finding: Field log of real analysts using GPT-4 (0613). Analysts used it as an on-demand aid for sensemaking and context-building, not for final high-stakes decisions. Most queries interpret low-level telemetry such as commands, or refine text.
numbers: 3,090 queries, 45 SOC analysts, 10 months; 93% of queries map to NICE framework competencies; most interactions 1-3 turns; mean query length 25 words (SD 70); understanding/analysis is the largest theme; active analysts grew from 4 (May 2023) to a peak of 25 (Feb 2024).
limits: One organisation; usage skewed to a few power users; no accuracy or outcome measure; GPT-4-0613 only.
agent_relevance: Real analysts hand the interpret-and-re-represent step to the model and keep the decision. Supports a scaffold where the model fills slots and code or a human decides.

source: Tang, Abulikemu, Krokos, Whitley & Wang (2025) Agentic reasoning and refinement through semantic interaction (VIS-ReAct)
finding: Treats the analyst workspace as a changing state: the LLM report is refined only where the user's highlights, notes or cluster moves changed (incremental formalism). Uses the Sign of the Crescent set (41 fictional intelligence reports, three attack plots). Cites P&C 2005. Compares full regeneration, targeted update (VIS-Act) and analyse-then-refine (VIS-ReAct).
numbers: 35 pairs of original and modified workspaces, 13 interaction combinations, 10-document plots. Targeted-refinement precision / recall: baseline 0.752 / 0.858; VIS-Act 0.975 / 0.782; VIS-ReAct 0.951 / 0.887. Semantic-fidelity table is garbled in the extract: precision 0.348 / 0.582 / 0.558 and one further row 0.694 / 0.526 / 0.684, last row 0.463 / 0.553 / 0.614; text says VIS-ReAct has best F1.
limits: Small test set made by the authors; paragraph-level ground truth; second table read with care. Authors note the LLM could not reliably find differences between two workspaces, so code does the diff.
agent_relevance: Diffing workspaces in code, then asking the model to edit only what changed, beat regeneration on precision. Fits G2 and 'code locates, model fills'.

source: Tang, Tahmid, Krokos, Whitley, Wang & North (2026) Semantic Prompting: agentic incremental narrative refinement through spatial semantic interaction (S-prism)
finding: Follow-up with a user study of spatial-layout steering of LLM reports. Incremental refinement gave steady gain in report correctness; a regeneration baseline plateaued and its variance grew on the hardest task.
numbers: N=14 participants (9 F, 5 M), about 90 minutes, two phases (4 guided closed-ended refinement tasks; 3 open-ended travel-planning scenarios). Completeness checked on 4 clusters, 9 keywords, 5 local insights, 2 global insights; regeneration omitted 4 of 9 keywords for one participant; 'attention dilution' when a big restructuring crowded out local edits.
limits: Small N, lab setting, non-intelligence content in Phase II, authors' own rubric. Highlights lacked positional meaning and were misread.
agent_relevance: Regenerating whole outputs loses earlier evidence as new text overshadows it; incremental edits against a persistent store keep it. Argues for a persistent evidence store.

source: Mooney, Kim, Lee & Kang (2026) Structure liberates: how constrained sensemaking produces more novel research output (SciSense)
finding: Turns the P&C stages into eight ordered stages for LLM research ideation: retrieve prior work and gaps, organise evidence, initial problem framing, testable hypotheses, method plan, feasibility and novelty check, revise, synthesise. Distils 120K trajectories into 3B-70B models. Outcome-anchored 'Hindsight' supervision beat open-ended 'Foresight'.
numbers: SciSense-Traj: 120,000 trajectories (50K/5K/5K per condition); eight open-weight backbones (Qwen3, Gemma-3, Llama-3). Hindsight gains 2.0% in aggregate plan quality over Foresight and is most diverse under every metric in all eight families. Judge check: Krippendorff alpha 0.70 among 3 humans, 0.69 with the LLM judge added (100 trajectories). Diversity from 5 trajectories for each of 100 held-out citation sets. GRPO gave small gains (overall 2.51 to 2.53 at 32B).
limits: Judge is an LLM; 2.0% is small; the eight-stage mapping from P&C is the authors' own operationalisation; this is training, not prompt-only scaffolding. Downstream coding-agent results sit in a figure that was not read as numbers.
agent_relevance: Closest LLM use of the P&C loop. Evidence that a staged sense scaffold can raise quality and diversity together, but the gain is from training on reconstructed paths, not from a runtime scaffold alone.

source: Mooney, Kim, Lee & Kang (2026) Structure liberates: how constrained sensemaking produces more novel research output (SciSense)
finding: Stage mix differs by supervision. Hindsight trajectories spend more on Schema (+4.2 points), Foraging (+3.7), Elaboration (+1.7); Foresight spends more on Hypothesis (+4.4) and Presentation (+2.1). Hindsight is schema-first and artifact-grounded; Foresight opens with a hypothesis.
numbers: Stage annotation of 1K generations per condition from the 32B model.
limits: Stage tagging done on model text; correlational.
agent_relevance: Hint that building a schema before hypothesising gives more grounded plans; matches the sense-loop order (schema then hypothesis).

source: Qian & Liu (2025) Scent of knowledge: optimizing search-enhanced reasoning with information foraging (InForage)
finding: RL framework that treats search-augmented reasoning as foraging (cites Pirolli & Card 1999): an information-gain reward for intermediate retrieval and an efficiency penalty. Beats baselines on QA, multi-hop and a new real-time web QA set with a 3B model.
numbers: Built on Qwen-2.5-3B-Instruct; RAG top-k=3. Ablations: removing the information-gain reward lowers scores on all datasets; removing the efficiency penalty hurts except on the self-built web set (long chains needed). Exact table values were not extracted.
limits: Trained model, not a scaffold; table numbers not read; own dataset built by the authors; the efficiency penalty is task-dependent.
agent_relevance: A foraging reward is a reward for retrieval quality at each step, not just the final answer. A per-step information-gain check is a code-computable signal for our foraging loop.

source: Jiang (2025) Workflow is all you need: escaping the statistical smoothing trap via high-entropy information foraging and adversarial pacing (DeepNews)
finding: Applies information foraging theory to financial-news writing: very wide retrieval (about 10:1 input-to-output) plus schema planning. Reports a 'knowledge cliff': truthfulness drops when retrieved context is under 15,000 characters.
numbers: Hallucination-free rate rises from 40% to about 85% above 30,000 characters of context. 40-day blind field test: DeepNews on DeepSeek-V3-0324 submitted 12 articles, 3 accepted (25%); GPT-5 with persona prompting submitted 10, 0 accepted. Cost per article about 0.7 vs 0.5 (currency symbol lost in extract).
limits: Single author, tiny counts (3 of 12 vs 0 of 10 is not a significant gap), one domain and outlet, thresholds in characters not tokens. Treat as suggestive only.
agent_relevance: Weak evidence that saturating the evidence pool before writing cuts unsupported claims. Replicate on our tasks before relying on it.

source: Cross-source note on replications and failures
finding: No direct replication of the P&C 2005 notional model was found. It is cited as a framework; the quantitative follow-ups here test downstream tools (Sensecape, Selenite, VIS-ReAct) or fit a task-level model (Lebiere 2013). Null result: Andrews (2011) large-display users built more structure but did not score significantly better.
numbers: P&C 2005 reports no N. Lebiere 2013 fits 45 then 103 participants. LLM tool studies use N=8 to 14.
limits: Search was limited this session (arXiv search page and a few fetches; Semantic Scholar and OpenAlex were rate-limited; WebSearch budget ran out). Absence of replications is not proven.
agent_relevance: Treat the loop as a design heuristic, not a validated mechanism. Use it to name states and transitions; test each ourselves.
